notes.text: **Genesis 27:28** — וְיִתֶּן לְךָ הָאֱלֹהִים מִטַּל הַשָּׁמַיִם וּמִשְׁמַנֵּי הָאָרֶץ וְרֹב דָּגָן וְתִירֹשׁ. Isaac asks that God grant Jacob heaven's dew, the richness of the soil, and an abundance of grain and new wine. Rav Tzadok reads the whole verse as a blessing that Jacob's eating itself be holy. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Toldot 8** (Rav Tzadok) — reads the same verse as bread and wine and brings the same halakhic proof that all five grains are “bread”, then goes further: the life in food is the “word of God” in it (Deuteronomy 8:3), with bread as the Written Torah and wine as the Oral Torah. *checked*

**Genesis 14:18** — וּמַלְכִּי צֶדֶק מֶלֶךְ שָׁלֵם הוֹצִיא לֶחֶם וָיָיִן וְהוּא כֹהֵן לְאֵל עֶלְיוֹן. Malki-Tzedek, king of Shalem and priest of the Most High, brings out bread and wine to Avram. The pairing shows that “grain and wine” in Isaac's blessing means bread and wine. *Mafteach: missing*

**Mishnah, Nedarim 55a** — הַנּוֹדֵר מִן הַדָּגָן... וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵינוֹ אָסוּר אֶלָּא בַּחֲמֵשֶׁת הַמִּינִין. Someone who vows off “dagan” is, according to the Sages, forbidden only the five grains. So in the language of people “dagan” means the five grains, which are bread. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Nedarim 38a; correct: Nedarim 55a)*

**Mishnah Challah 1:1–2** — חֲמִשָּׁה דְבָרִים חַיָּבִים בַּחַלָּה... הָאוֹכֵל מֵהֶם כַּזַּיִת מַצָּה בְּפֶסַח יָצָא יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ... הַנּוֹדֵר מִן הַדָּגָן אֵינוֹ אָסוּר אֶלָּא מֵהֶן. The same five grains are the ones liable to challah and the ones that can be matzah, and the same Mishnah also rules on the vow against “dagan”. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Challah, no chapter or mishnah given; correct: Mishnah Challah 1:2)*

**Genesis 27:37** — הֵן גְּבִיר שַׂמְתִּיו לָךְ וְאֶת כָּל אֶחָיו נָתַתִּי לוֹ לַעֲבָדִים וְדָגָן וְתִירֹשׁ סְמַכְתִּיו. Isaac tells Esau: I have made him your master and made his brothers his servants, and I have supported him with grain and wine. Rav Tzadok reads סְמַכְתִּיו as “I have braced him”, so that plenty will not harm him. *Mafteach: found*

**Bereshit Rabbah 67:5** — הֵן גְּבִיר שַׂמְתִּיו לָךְ, בְּרָכָה שְׁבִיעִית, וְלָמָה הוּא אוֹמְרָהּ לוֹ תְּחִלָּה? אֶלָּא אָמַר לוֹ: מֶלֶךְ עֲשִׂיתִיהוּ עָלֶיךָ וּבִרְכוֹתֶיךָ שֶׁלּוֹ הֵן... עַבְדָּא כָּל מַה דִּילֵיהּ לְמָרָא. “Master” was the seventh blessing, yet Isaac mentions it first. The reason: once Jacob is king over you, your own blessings are his too, since whatever a slave has belongs to his master. *Mafteach: found*

**Rashi on Genesis 27:28** — הָאֱלֹהִים, בַּדִּין: אִם רָאוּי לְךָ יִתֵּן לְךָ, וְאִם לָאו לֹא יִתֵּן לְךָ; אֲבָל לְעֵשָׂו אָמַר... בֵּין צַדִּיק בֵּין רָשָׁע יִתֵּן לְךָ. The Name Elohim means judgment: Jacob receives only if he deserves it, while Esau's blessing does not depend on merit. Rashi on 27:40 states the consequence: כְּשֶׁיַּעַבְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל הַתּוֹרָה וְיִהְיֶה לְךָ פִּתְחוֹן פֶּה, which is exactly the claim Rav Tzadok puts in Esau's mouth. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Akeidat Yitzchak 24:1:13** (Machshava) — Arama also reads “Elohim” as the attribute of judgment, so Jacob's blessings are conditional and Esau's are not. He also reads סְמַכְתִּיו as supports that hold up a greater good, the same verse Rav Tzadok turns into Isaac's answer.
אמנם הזכיר בכאן אלהים שהוא דיין בכל מקום להורות שלא נתנו הברכות רק אל הטוב בעיני האלהים

**Sifrei Devarim 43 (Ekev)** — הִזָּהֲרוּ שֶׁמָּא תִּמְרְדוּ בַּמָּקוֹם! שֶׁאֵין אָדָם מוֹרֵד בַּמָּקוֹם אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ שׂוֹבַע. On “you will eat and be satisfied; take care” (Deuteronomy 11:15–16): rebellion against God grows only out of being full. The Sifrei proves it from the generation of the Flood, the Tower and Sodom. *Mafteach: missing*

**Berakhot 32a** — אֵין אֲרִי נוֹהֵם מִתּוֹךְ קוּפָּה שֶׁל תֶּבֶן אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ קוּפָּה שֶׁל בָּשָׂר... מְלֵי כְּרֵסֵיהּ זְנֵי בִּישֵׁי. A lion roars from a basket of meat, not from a basket of straw, and a full stomach leads to sin. The Gemara applies this to the silver and gold that led to the Golden Calf (“וְדִי זָהָב”) and brings the verses “וַיִּשְׁמַן יְשֻׁרוּן וַיִּבְעָט” and “וְרָם לְבָבֶךָ וְשָׁכַחְתָּ”. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels:** **Divrei Chalomot 5** (Rav Tzadok) — the same chain (Tanna DeBei Eliyahu 26, Tosafot Ketubot 104a, Berakhot 32a “מלי כריסי”), with a note on how Tosafot's wording differs from the Tanna DeBei Eliyahu. It adds that sanctifying one's eating is “the beginning of chassidus”. *checked*
**Peri Tzadik, Masei 12** (Rav Tzadok) — brings the same three sources together with the Sifrei and adds two steps from this os: the Ari's ruling on Shabbos eating, and scholars who “resemble Shabbos”. It reads “כִּי תִשְׁמְרֵם בְּבִטְנֶךָ” (Proverbs 22:18) as holy eating that opens the heart to da'as. *checked*

**Tosafot, Ketubot 104a** (s.v. לא נהניתי אפילו באצבע קטנה) — דְּאָמְרִינַן בְּמִדְרָשׁ: עַד שֶׁאָדָם מִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁיִּכָּנֵס תּוֹרָה לְתוֹךְ גּוּפוֹ יִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּנְסוּ מַעֲדַנִּים לְתוֹךְ גּוּפוֹ. Tosafot cite this Midrash to explain Rebbi's deathbed words that he had not enjoyed this world even with his little finger. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Ketubot, no daf given; correct: Tosafot, Ketubot 104a)*

**Tanna DeBei Eliyahu Rabbah 26** — וְאִם לֹא זָכָה אָדָם לְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁיִּכָּנְסוּ לְתוֹךְ מֵעָיו, מִכָּל מָקוֹם יְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים עַל אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה יְתֵרָה שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּנְסוּ לְתוֹךְ מֵעָיו. If a person has not merited to pray that Torah enter him, he should at least pray that excess food and drink not enter him. The passage then tells of Rebbi's deathbed declaration, the story Tosafot have in mind. *Mafteach: wrong label (index: Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 5)*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Toldot 8** (Rav Tzadok) — the next os makes the same point from the same Zohar (I 143b). Esau's blessing is not phrased as God's gift and leaves out grain and wine, because these allude to the eternal life (Torah) within food, and Esau has no share in that. *checked*

**Zohar I 143b (Toldot)** — בְּיַעֲקֹב כְּתִיב וְיִתֶּן לְךָ הָאֱלֹהִים, וּבְדָא כְּתִיב יִהְיֶה. בְּיַעֲקֹב כְּתִיב מִטַּל הַשָּׁמַיִם וּמִשְׁמַנֵּי הָאָרֶץ, בְּעֵשָׂו כְּתִיב מִשְׁמַנֵּי הָאָרֶץ וְטַל הַשָּׁמַיִם. Rabbi Shimon: the two blessings are not alike. Jacob's is “God will give”, Esau's only “will be”, and even the order of dew and earth is reversed. *Mafteach: found*

**Genesis 27:39** — הִנֵּה מִשְׁמַנֵּי הָאָרֶץ יִהְיֶה מוֹשָׁבֶךָ וּמִטַּל הַשָּׁמַיִם מֵעָל. Esau's blessing: your dwelling will be in the rich places of the earth and under heaven's dew. It does not say “God will give” and it does not mention grain and wine, the two points Rav Tzadok builds on. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Genesis 27:40; correct: Genesis 27:39)*

**Genesis 27:40** — וְעַל חַרְבְּךָ תִחְיֶה וְאֶת אָחִיךָ תַּעֲבֹד וְהָיָה כַּאֲשֶׁר תָּרִיד וּפָרַקְתָּ עֻלּוֹ מֵעַל צַוָּארֶךָ. You will live by your sword and serve your brother; and when you break loose, you will throw his yoke off your neck. Rav Tzadok makes serving Jacob Esau's own completion. *Mafteach: found*

**Bereshit Rabbah 67:7** — וְעַל חַרְבְּךָ תִחְיֶה, רַבִּי לֵוִי אָמַר: עוּל חַרְבָּךְ וְאַתְּ חָיֵי. Rabbi Levi: put your sword under a yoke, and you will live. The same section gives other readings of the verse: Rav Huna's “if he merits, he will serve; if not, he will destroy”, and Rabbi Yose ben Chalafta's “when you see your brother throwing off the yoke of Torah”. Rav Tzadok's own reading of תָּרִיד as descent (1.46) differs from Rashi's “anguish”. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Be'er Mayim Chaim, Genesis 27:37** (Chassidus) — R. Chaim of Czernowitz has Isaac explain that even the blessing he meant for Esau was a this-worldly blessing on his labor, so that Esau would prepare Jacob's bread and be rectified through him. This is Rav Tzadok's “your life is to serve your brother”, and like him he reads “וְדָגָן וְתִירֹשׁ סְמַכְתִּיו” as the core of the blessing reserved for Jacob.
בכדי שתהיה אתה המכין לחם ליעקב להיות מלאכתו נעשית על ידך ואתה תתוקן על ידו

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Torat HaOlah, Part Two 18** (Machshava) — R. Moshe Isserles counts the same ten blessings, item by item, from “dew of heaven” to “those who bless you are blessed”. He links them to other tens: the ten things created at twilight on the eve of the first Shabbos, and the two tenths of flour brought with a ram.
שני עשרונים לאיל נגד עשרה ברכות שבירך יצחק את יעקב

**Parallels:** **Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Genesis, Toldot 5** (Ishbitz–Radzin) — the Izhbitzer also sets Isaac's blessings against the Ten Commandments, word by word (“וְיִתֶּן” = Anochi, “לְךָ” = Lo yihyeh lecha, “מִטַּל הַשָּׁמַיִם” = Shabbos …). He cites the same Zohar (Toldot 143b) for blessings that are “above, above”. Rav Tzadok maps the same ten onto the sefiros instead. *checked*

**Peri Tzadik, Chayei Sara 2** (Rav Tzadok) — וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנִּזְכָּר מִסְפַּר עֲשָׂרָה מְרַמֵּז כְּנֶגֶד עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת... וַעֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת כְּנֶגֶד ע"ס. There he explains why the children of Ches are named ten times: every ten points to the Ten Commandments, the ten utterances of Creation and the ten sefiros. The same essay also sets out the six “groomsmen” attributes (Moshe and Aharon as Netzach and Hod, Yaakov and Yosef as one), which is the scheme of paragraph 3. *Mafteach: missing*

**Zohar III 128b (Idra Rabba)** — נָטִיף טַלָּא מֵרֵישָׁא חִיוָּורָא, דְּאִתְמְלֵּי מִנֵיהּ תָּדִיר; וּמֵהַאי טַלָּא דְּאַנְעַר מֵרֵישֵׁיהּ זְמִינִין מֵיתַיָּיא לְאַחֲיָּאָה. Dew drips from the “white head” of Atika, and through that dew the dead will be revived (Isaiah 26:19, “כִּי טַל אוֹרֹת טַלֶּךָ”). Rav Tzadok does not give an address; this is the Idra passage on the dew of Atika, which stands for Keter, on III 128b (Idra Rabba, Sefaria 4:1-2). *Mafteach: missing (now added)*

**Zohar III 243b**, as Rav Tzadok gives it — Malchus called “the land of life” and “the land of the Holy One”. The words were not found on III 243b in Sefaria's page division (Pinchas, Ra'aya Mehemna). The pairing appears in **Zohar, Pinchas (Sefaria 41:2; III 222b–224a)**: אֶרֶץ, אֶרֶץ קַדִּישָׁא עִילָּאָה, אֶרֶץ הַחַיִּים, and the name itself in **Zohar, Bereshit (Sefaria 39:392)**: וְקָרִינָן לֵיהּ מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם וְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֶרֶץ הַחַיִּים. *Mafteach: missing*

**Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Patach Eliyahu)** — כֶּתֶר עִלְיוֹן אִיהוּ כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת, וַעֲלֵיהּ אִתְּמַר מַגִּיד מֵרֵאשִׁית אַחֲרִית. The supreme Crown is itself the crown of Malchus, the first sefirah joined to the last. That is why Isaac pairs “dew of heaven” (Keter) with “the richness of the earth” (Malchus). *Mafteach: missing*

**Isaiah 46:10** — מַגִּיד מֵרֵאשִׁית אַחֲרִית וּמִקֶּדֶם אֲשֶׁר לֹא נַעֲשׂוּ. God declares the end from the beginning. Patach Eliyahu reads the verse as the end contained in the beginning, Malchus in Keter. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Maggid Meisharim 5:5–6** (Kabbalah) — R. Yosef Karo's maggid gives Rav Tzadok's mapping exactly: heaven's dew is Keter, grain is Chokhmah (“called bread”), new wine is Binah. In the same passage “let peoples serve you” refers to the seventy princes, and Jacob's blessings are “above, above” while Esau's are “below, below”.
דטל השמים רמיז לכתר. ודגן רמיז לחכמה דאיקרי לחם. ותירוש רמז לבינה

**Ecclesiastes 7:12** — כִּי בְּצֵל הַחָכְמָה בְּצֵל הַכָּסֶף וְיִתְרוֹן דַּעַת הַחָכְמָה תְּחַיֶּה בְעָלֶיהָ. Wisdom gives life to those who have it. Wisdom gives life the way bread does, so grain stands for Chokhmah. *Mafteach: missing*

**Deuteronomy 8:3** — כִּי לֹא עַל הַלֶּחֶם לְבַדּוֹ יִחְיֶה הָאָדָם כִּי עַל כָּל מוֹצָא פִי ה' יִחְיֶה הָאָדָם. A person does not live on bread alone but on everything that comes out of God's mouth. Rav Tzadok takes “מוֹצָא פִי ה'” as the word of God inside the bread itself. *Mafteach: missing*

**Zohar III 271b (Ekev, Ra'aya Mehemna)** — לְכוּ לַחֲמוּ בְּלַחְמִי, וְדָא נַהֲמָא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דְּבִכְתָב, וְיֵינָא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דִּבְעַל פֶּה. “Come, eat my bread” is the bread of the Written Torah, and the wine is the Oral Torah. The passage is in the Ra'aya Mehemna on Ekev; the Vilna page marker רעא: comes just before it. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Zohar III 266b; correct: Zohar III 271b)*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Toldot 8** (Rav Tzadok) — the same Zohar (III 271b) applied to Isaac's blessing. Wheat (חִטָּה) has the numerical value 22, the letters of the Torah, and the Midrash's mikra/mishnah/talmud/aggadah reading of dew, earth, grain and wine is explained. *checked*
**Peri Tzadik, Rosh Chodesh Shvat 5** (Rav Tzadok) — eating “as before the sin”, when the food of Adam was “לְכוּ לַחֲמוּ בְּלַחְמִי נַהֲמָא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דְּבִכְתָב”. In the same passage: scholars who resemble Shabbos and the Ari on holy Shabbos eating. *checked*

**Proverbs 2:6** — כִּי ה' יִתֵּן חָכְמָה מִפִּיו דַּעַת וּתְבוּנָה. God gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding. The first half is Chokhmah as a direct gift (“plenty of grain”). Rav Tzadok returns to the second half at 2.17 for Binah, the Oral Torah drawn out by understanding. *Mafteach: found*

**Psalms 104:15** — וְיַיִן יְשַׂמַּח לְבַב אֱנוֹשׁ... וְלֶחֶם לְבַב אֱנוֹשׁ יִסְעָד. Wine gladdens the heart and bread sustains it. Wine belongs to the heart, which is where Binah sits (next note). *Mafteach: found*

**Tikkunei Zohar, Introduction 17a (Patach Eliyahu)** — חָכְמָה מוֹחָא אִיהִי מַחְשָׁבָה מִלְּגָאו, בִּינָה לִבָּא וּבָהּ הַלֵּב מֵבִין. Chokhmah is the brain, inner thought; Binah is the heart, and through it the heart understands. *Mafteach: missing*

**Chagigah 14a** — וְנָבוֹן, זֶה הַמֵּבִין דָּבָר מִתּוֹךְ דָּבָר; similarly **Sanhedrin 93b** on David, “וּנְבוֹן דָּבָר שֶׁמֵּבִין דָּבָר מִתּוֹךְ דָּבָר”. The understanding person derives one thing from another, which is how the Oral Torah is drawn out of the Written. *Mafteach: missing*

**Proverbs 9:5** — לְכוּ לַחֲמוּ בְלַחֲמִי וּשְׁתוּ בְּיַיִן מָסָכְתִּי. Wisdom's invitation: eat my bread, drink the wine I have mixed. In the Zohar quoted at 2.11 the mixed wine is the Oral Torah. *Mafteach: found*

**Genesis 27:29** — יַעַבְדוּךָ עַמִּים וְיִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְךָ לְאֻמִּים הֱוֵה גְבִיר לְאַחֶיךָ וְיִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְךָ בְּנֵי אִמֶּךָ אֹרְרֶיךָ אָרוּר וּמְבָרְכֶיךָ בָּרוּךְ. These are the six this-worldly blessings that paragraph 3 assigns to the six shepherds. *Mafteach: found*

**Bereshit Rabbah 66:6**; **Yerushalmi Berakhot 8:8** — עוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים אֶחָד פָּגַע בְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, בֵּרְכוֹ, אָמַר לוֹ: כְּבָר מִלָּתְךָ אֲמוּרָה. פָּגַע בּוֹ אֶחָד וְקִלְלוֹ, אָמַר לוֹ: כְּבָר מִלָּתְךָ אֲמוּרָה... כֵּן כְּתִיב: מְבָרְכֶיךָ בָּרוּךְ אֹרְרֶיךָ אָרוּר. A gentile blessed Rabbi Yishmael and another cursed him, and he gave both the same reply: “your word has already been said”. Scripture has already settled the fate of those who bless or curse Israel, so the last pair of blessings concerns the nations. *Mafteach: missing*

**Isaiah 61:5** — וְעָמְדוּ זָרִים וְרָעוּ צֹאנְכֶם וּבְנֵי נֵכָר אִכָּרֵיכֶם וְכֹרְמֵיכֶם. Strangers will tend your flocks and foreigners will be your farmers and vinedressers. This is the future “remnant” of the nations who bless Israel and are blessed through serving it. *Mafteach: found*

**The Arizal, on Shabbat eating** — Rav Tzadok cites without a place that whatever a Jew eats on Shabbat, even for his own enjoyment, is holy; in Rosh Chodesh Shvat 3 he gives it as אִיתָא מֵהָאֲרִ״י ... שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל אוֹכֵל בְּשַׁבָּת, אַף לַהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ, הוּא בִּקְדוּשָּׁה. The exact passage in the Arizal's writings was not found in Pri Etz Chaim, Etz Chaim, Sha'ar HaKavanot or Sha'ar HaMitzvot as searched. The same teaching is quoted in his name by later Chassidus: **Shem MiShmuel, Beshalach 3** “אִיתָא בְּכִתְבֵי הָאֲרִ״י שֶׁמַּאֲכַל שַׁבָּת אֵינוֹ מְגַשֵּׁם”, and Korach and Ki Teitzei there. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Toldot 10** (Rav Tzadok) — reads the same six blessings (“יַעַבְדוּךָ עַמִּים”) as this-worldly aids given “לשם שמים”, and cites the Ari that Shabbos pleasure is holy even for oneself. It adds that the higher level is still to delight the extra soul, which is why the Gemara says “המענג את השבת”. *checked*
**Peri Tzadik, Rosh Chodesh Shvat 5** (Rav Tzadok) — Shevat as the time to repair the serpent's damage to eating, so that weekday eating becomes like Shabbos eating “אף כשהגוף נהנה”, and the eating of scholars “דדמיין לשבתות”. *checked*

**Zohar III 124b–125a (Naso, Ra'aya Mehemna)** — אִינּוּן חֲכָמִים דְּדַמְיָין לְשַׁבָּתוֹת וְיוֹם טוֹב, לֵית לוֹן אֶלָּא מַה דְּיָהֲבִין לוֹן אִינּוּן חוּלִין, כְּגַוְונָא דְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת. Scholars are like Shabbos and festivals: they have only what the weekday people give them, as Shabbos has only what is prepared during the week. The Vilna marker for 125a falls in the middle of this sentence, which fits Rav Tzadok's “end of 124b”. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Tanya, Iggeret HaKodesh 26** (Chassidus) — R. Shneur Zalman quotes the same Ra'aya Mehemna. In the era of the tree of good and evil, scholars who “resemble Shabbos” are sustained by the weekday world, yet their food comes from the side of the tree of life, so the weekday is lifted to a Shabbos sanctity.
אִינוּן חֲכָמִים דְּדַמְיָין לְשַׁבָּתוֹת וְיָמִים טוֹבִים, לֵית לְהוֹן, אֶלָּא מַה דְיָהֲבִין לְהוֹן אִינּוּן ״חוּלִּין״

**Berakhot 34b** — קִידָּה עַל אַפַּיִם... כְּרִיעָה עַל בִּרְכַּיִם... הִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה זוֹ פִּשּׁוּט יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם. Kidah is on the face, keri'ah on the knees, and hishtachava'ah is lying stretched out with hands and feet spread. The same baraita appears in Megillah 22b and Shevuot 16b. Rav Tzadok: full prostration means the whole body is surrendered. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Sulam on Zohar, Toldot 139** (Kabbalah) — R. Yehuda Ashlag also reads the blessings as stages of the final rectification. Dew and the richness of the earth are Z"A and Nukva, grain and wine are the mochin called bread and wine, and “be master over your brothers” makes Esau's path an aid to Jacob's, like a servant helping his master.
הוה גביר לאחיך שהדרך שלך ישאר לנצחיות, והדרך של אחיך יהיה לך למסייע, כמו עבד המסייע לאדונו

**Peri Tzadik, Toldot 6** (Rav Tzadok) — וְהַיְינוּ דְּיַעֲקֹב וְעֵשָׂו זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה עָשָׂה אֱלֹהִים. Jacob, whose trait is truth, uses cunning only against the deceiver, and so draws the blessings away from “that serpent”. Esau's kelipah is malchus of wickedness and the source of Amalek, “ראשית דקליפה”, the phrase that returns at 3.21. *Mafteach: missing*

**Tikkunei Zohar 29a (Tikkun 13)** — וְיַעֲקֹב וַדַּאי אִיהוּ דִיּוֹקְנָא דְעַמּוּדָא דְאֶמְצָעִיתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִּלְבָר, וְהָא מֹשֶׁה תַמָּן הֲוָה, אֶלָּא מִסִּטְרָא דִלְגָאו הֲוָה, דָּא מִגּוּפָא וְדָא מִנִּשְׁמָתָא. Jacob is the image of the Central Pillar from outside, Moses from inside: one its body, the other its soul. The same passage goes on to Netzach and Hod as the two thighs of the Central Pillar, which is why Moses is the chariot of Netzach. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Tikkunei Zohar 33 (and a second entry, Tikkunei Zohar 69); correct: Tikkunei Zohar 29a, Tikkun 13)*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Shenei Luchot HaBerit, Vayetzei, Torah Ohr 28** (Mussar/Kabbalah) — the Shelah explains the same Tikkunim saying. Jacob is the chariot of Tiferes in its revealed place and Moses of its hidden inner aspect, Da'as. This supports Rav Tzadok's point that the inner dimension, Moses, is what nullifies Esau completely.
יעקב הוא מרכבה לתפארת במקומו הנגלה, ומשה מרכבה להנעלם של התפארת שהוא הדעת

**Isaiah 60:21** — וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים לְעוֹלָם יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ. All your people are righteous; they will inherit the land forever. The Zohar in the next note reads “righteous” here as circumcised. *Mafteach: missing*

**Zohar II 23a (Va'era)** — וְכָל מַאן דְּאִתְגְּזַר אִקְרֵי צַדִּיק, דִּכְתִּיב וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים... תָּא חֲזֵי מִן יוֹסֵף, דְּכָל יוֹמוֹי לָא אִקְרֵי צַדִּיק עַד דְּנָטִיר הַהוּא בְּרִית. Whoever is circumcised is called a tzaddik. Joseph was called “the tzaddik” only once he had guarded the covenant, which is why Joseph is the chariot of Yesod. *Mafteach: missing*

**Midrash Tanchuma, Ki Teitzei 10** — מֶה הָיוּ בֵּית עֲמָלֵק עוֹשִׂין? חוֹתְכִין מִילוֹתֵיהֶן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְזוֹרְקִין כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה וְאוֹמְרִין: בָּזֶה בָּחַרְתָּ, הֱוֵי לְךָ מַה שֶּׁבָּחַרְתָּ. Amalek cut off the circumcised members and threw them heavenward, saying “take what You chose”. The Tanchuma adds that Esau falls only by the hand of Rachel's children, Joseph's tribe (Joshua), which fits Rav Tzadok's Joseph–Amalek pairing. *Mafteach: missing*

**Pirkei Avot 1:12** — הִלֵּל אוֹמֵר: הֱוֵי מִתַּלְמִידָיו שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן, אוֹהֵב שָׁלוֹם וְרוֹדֵף שָׁלוֹם, אוֹהֵב אֶת הַבְּרִיּוֹת וּמְקָרְבָן לַתּוֹרָה. Hillel: be a disciple of Aaron, loving peace and pursuing it, loving people and drawing them close to Torah. *Mafteach: missing*

**Isaiah 61:6** — וְאַתֶּם כֹּהֲנֵי ה' תִּקָּרֵאוּ מְשָׁרְתֵי אֱלֹהֵינוּ יֵאָמֵר לָכֶם. You will be called priests of God, ministers of our God. The verse comes right after “strangers will tend your flocks” (2.28): Israel as priests, the nations serving them. *Mafteach: found*
**Exodus 19:6** — וְאַתֶּם תִּהְיוּ לִי מַמְלֶכֶת כֹּהֲנִים וְגוֹי קָדוֹשׁ. At Sinai all Israel is called a kingdom of priests, which is drawn from Aaron's holiness. *Mafteach: found*

**Proverbs 22:9** — טוֹב עַיִן הוּא יְבֹרָךְ כִּי נָתַן מִלַּחְמוֹ לַדָּל. The generous of eye will be blessed, for he gives of his bread to the poor. Aaron, the priest who blesses, is the one through whom blessing flows into the world. *Mafteach: found*
